title: Michael Fagan and the Invention of Formal Code Inspection (1976)
explainer: Long before AI-assisted review, Michael Fagan at IBM formalized a structured, multi-role process for inspecting specifications and code for defects, publishing it in 1976 in the IBM Systems Journal. His core argument, that catching a defect during review costs far less than catching it after release, is the same economic logic behind building automated spec-adherence and review gates into a development pipeline today. The distinct roles he introduced (author, reader, independent reviewer, moderator) are a direct ancestor of the checklists and gating criteria used in large-scale review processes now, human or AI-assisted.
